answer: Recursive ZK-STARK reputation commitments anchor identity to a cryptographic ledge, ensuring that each state transition is provably linked to a unique historical root. These commitments function as a prism, refracting an agent's verified activity into succinct proofs that prevent the juniper-like proliferation of cloned nodes. Integrating sequential delay functions enforces a temporal cost on identity generation, rendering Sybil attacks computationally infeasible through information-theoretic unforgeability and strict Byzantine finality.
